content:

Tigrayans in northern Ethiopia have begun panic buying supplies as the region’s months of tension appear to have escalated into a full‑blown conflict, according to the latest report. The surge in stock‑piling reflects growing fears among residents that hostilities could intensify at any moment.

In other news, power cuts have returned to Senegal, disrupting electricity service across the country. Meanwhile, Nigerian superstar Yemis Alade has released a new album and discussed the project in an interview with France 24.

The report notes that Tigrayans are panic buying supplies amid fears of full‑blown conflict, power cuts have returned to Senegal, and Yemis Alade is out with a new album and speaks to France 24.
author: France 24

title: Iran Airlines Suspended, Land Routes Strained by US Sanctions
content:
Flights between Iran and the United Arab Emirates have been suspended after the United States tightened sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry, effectively cutting Tehran off from Dubai, one of the region’s most important commercial hubs. The move has triggered significant disruptions in both air and land travel, with large backups reported near Iran’s border with Turkey as overland shipping routes struggle to compensate for the loss of air connections.

The suspension has left Iranian passengers and freight stranded, and the backlog of cargo at the Turkey‑Iran border underscores the strain on alternative logistics corridors. The sanctions have also prompted a broader reassessment of travel and trade links across the region, as businesses and governments seek to navigate the new restrictions.

Flights between Iran and the UAE have been suspended, and overland routes near the Turkey border are experiencing large backups.
author: France 24

title: Macron denies CIA warned of Russian drone attacks
content:
French President Emmanuel Macron denied on Thursday that the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments of possible Russian drone attacks coming from the Mediterranean, a claim reported by the Spanish newspaper El Mundo. The denial was issued during a primetime television interview.

In the same interview, Macron announced that France would deploy troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help safeguard the Red Sea port city of Yanbu. The move is aimed at bolstering security in the region amid growing concerns over potential drone threats.

Macron denied the CIA warning report and stated that France will send troops and defence systems to Yanbu.
author: France 24

title: UN monitors report Russian attacks kill civilians and damage infrastructure in Ukraine
content:
World News in Brief reports a “new intensity” to Russian attacks, offering updates on Ukraine, Yemen, Gaza and Colombia. The summary highlights the heightened activity of Russian armed forces and the broader impact of the conflict across multiple regions.

According to UN human rights monitors, Russian forces have carried out repeated attacks across Ukraine over the past several days. The assaults have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries and have damaged homes, hospitals, shops and workplaces.

UN human rights monitors said on Thursday that the attacks have killed and injured civilians and damaged civilian infrastructure.
author: UN News

title: UNRWA's work and mandate in jeopardy, says UN Secretary-General
content:
UN Secretary‑General António Guterres warned that the work and mandate of the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine refugees (UNRWA) are in jeopardy, citing growing challenges to its operations.  

He said that UNRWA continues to operate under “extraordinary pressure,” a statement he made on Thursday.  

UNRWA continues to operate under extraordinary pressure, according to António Guterres.
author: UN News

title: Haitian Prime Minister says citizens eager to return home and vote
content:
Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils‑Aimé told a special United Nations meeting on the future of security in Haiti that the Haitian people “can’t wait to return home and vote in elections.” The statement highlighted the urgency felt by citizens to regain normalcy and participate in the democratic process.

Fils‑Aimé added that the population is eager to “regain security, to return home to work, to send their children to school, and to freely choose their leaders.” The remarks were made during the UN gathering focused on Haiti’s security situation.
author: UN News

title: Tigrayan forces claim full‑blown war with Ethiopian army
content:
The latest surge of violence in Ethiopia has been linked to statements from Tigrayan forces, who assert that they are now engaged in a “full‑blown war” with the national army. This claim highlights a significant escalation in the conflict between the two sides.

Tigrayan representatives maintain that the fighting has reached the level of a full‑blown war with the army, underscoring the heightened intensity of the hostilities. Tigrayan forces say they are in a “full‑blown war” with the army.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel election panel votes to disqualify main Palestinian-led lists
content:
Israel’s election panel has voted to disqualify the two main Palestinian‑led lists from the upcoming vote. The decision was taken as the country prepares for the election scheduled for next month.

The panel’s ruling means that the two principal Palestinian‑led political groupings will be barred from participating in that election, removing them from the ballot.

The election panel voted to disqualify the two main Palestinian‑led lists from next month’s election.
author: Al Jazeera

title: New York sues Polymarket over alleged illegal gambling operations
content:
New York has filed a lawsuit against Polymarket, alleging that the platform operates illegal gambling activities. The legal action targets the company’s operations and seeks to address the state’s concerns about compliance with gambling regulations.

The suit follows a similar lawsuit the state filed two months earlier against Polymarket’s competitor Kalshi, marking a continued effort by New York to enforce gambling laws against digital prediction markets. The state has now taken legal action against both Polymarket and Kalshi.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US citizen injured after wrongful ICE arrest in Illinois
content:
A US citizen was injured after being wrongly arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Illinois.  

The incident took place in Illinois, where ICE detained the individual despite the person’s US citizenship, leading to an injury during the arrest.  

The US citizen was injured after the wrongful ICE arrest in Illinois.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Netanyahu blames juvenile delinquents for West Bank violence
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blamed “juvenile delinquents” for the violence occurring in the occupied West Bank. In his remarks, he attributed the unrest to these individuals rather than other factors.

Speaking at the United Nations, Netanyahu downplayed settler violence in the occupied West Bank while making the accusation against juvenile delinquents. Netanyahu made the remarks at the United Nations, attributing the violence to juvenile delinquents and downplaying settler involvement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Portugal beats Wales 1-0 with Joao Felix goal
content:
Portugal began its Nations League defence with a 1-0 victory over Wales, secured by a single goal from Joao Felix. The match saw Cristiano Ronaldo have an effort ruled out, but the Portuguese side held on to the narrow lead.

The win was achieved through Felix’s decisive strike, while Ronaldo’s attempt was disallowed, resulting in Portugal’s 1-0 win over Wales. Portugal defeated Wales 1-0 with Joao Felix’s goal, while Cristiano Ronaldo’s effort was ruled out.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Dutch PM Rob Jetten backs Netanyahu's UNGA attendance despite ICC warrant
content:
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten has drawn attention for taking a contrasting approach toward two leaders subject to International Criminal Court actions, namely Russian President Vladimir Putin and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The distinction in his positions is highlighted by his recent comments regarding Netanyahu’s participation in an upcoming United Nations General Assembly session.

Jetten said that Netanyahu should be allowed to attend the UNGA despite the existence of an ICC arrest warrant against the Israeli premier. This statement underscores the Dutch leader’s differing stance on the two ICC‑wanted figures.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder arrested at UN protest before Netanyahu speech
content:
Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder were arrested at a protest outside the United Nations headquarters ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s scheduled speech. The arrests occurred as demonstrators gathered to voice opposition to the upcoming address.

Both actors were among roughly 100 protesters taken into custody outside the UN before Netanyahu’s speech began.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Italy ministers approve school ban on burqa, niqab and limit foreign student numbers
content:
Italy ministers have agreed to prohibit the wearing of burqa and niqab in schools and to introduce a limit on the number of foreign students in each class. The policy aims to regulate attire and classroom composition within the national education system.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the measures as “common‑sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate.” The prime minister’s comment underscores the government’s view that the steps are intended to promote integration.
author: BBC World

title: Priest killed and four injured in knife attack at Polish abbey, suspect arrested
content:
A priest was killed and four people were injured in a knife attack at a Polish abbey in the town of Jarosław, police reported. The incident involved multiple stabbings at the religious site, resulting in the fatality of the clergyman and injuries to four others.

Police said a male suspect from Ukraine was arrested after the stabbings in Jarosław. The arrest was confirmed by authorities following the attack.
author: BBC World

title: Taliban reports four civilian deaths in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan
content:
Four civilians were killed in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan, the Taliban reported.  

Pakistan said its forces hit ten targets and described the operations as “strictly limited to identified military objectives.” The incident involved four civilian deaths and ten targets that Pakistan says were military objectives.
author: BBC World

title: Netanyahu defends Israeli actions at UN as delegates walk out
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used a United Nations platform to defend Israel’s military actions in the Middle East. His remarks formed the centerpiece of a speech that attracted significant attention from the international delegation.

During the address, dozens of delegates walked out in protest as Netanyahu took the podium, and he responded by labeling the departing representatives “moral cowards.” The walkout and his description of the delegates occurred during his UN speech.
author: BBC World

title: Seth Meyers on Trump’s praise of Xi Jinping: ‘Not even Chinese citizens gush this much about Xi’
content:
Late-night hosts have discussed Donald Trump’s unusually lavish state reception for visiting Chinese leader Xi Jinping, with Seth Meyers specifically criticizing the president’s effusive remarks. Meyers commented on the intensity of Trump’s praise by stating, “Not even Chinese citizens gush this much about Xi.” The segment also addressed the political context of the event, noting that the discussion included Republicans’ desperate efforts to save their chances in the midterms.

The late-night reaction focused on the contrast between the lavish nature of the state reception and the typical diplomatic protocol, highlighting the hosts' skepticism toward the administration's handling of the visit. This coverage serves as a commentary on the intersection of foreign policy and domestic political strategy during the ongoing midterm election cycle.
author: Guardian Culture

title: BBC upholds complaints over Victoria Beckham slur on Have I Got News For You
content:
Two viewers submitted complaints to the BBC regarding a "gratuitously offensive" comment made during an episode of *Have I Got News For You*. The complaints specifically addressed a slur involving Victoria Beckham that was aired on the program.

The BBC has upheld the complaints made by the two viewers concerning the incident.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Alcaraz leads Laver Cup return to London amid financial challenges
content:
The Laver Cup, a Ryder Cup-style tennis event, is set to return to London with Carlos Alcaraz headlining the lineup, aiming to demonstrate its value despite financial struggles following the retirement of its founder, Roger Federer. While the tournament continues to offer a unique spectacle in the sport, its economic stability has been challenged since Federer stepped away from his role.

The event’s intensity is illustrated by an anecdote from Prague nine years ago, where Alexander Zverev walked back to the locker room between sets flanked by Federer and another legendary player. During this walk, Federer reportedly instructed Zverev to fistpump or shout “Let’s go!” after winning points and to handle losses with dignity, criticizing his tendency to express frustration when results were unfavorable.
author: Guardian Sport

title: UK Football Policing Unit Criticized for Linking Hillsborough to Alcohol Debate
content:
The Football Supporters’ Association has accused the UK Football Policing Unit of “bringing Hillsborough into the debate” concerning proposals to allow fans to drink in sight of the pitch. The criticism follows remarks by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who described current rules prohibiting alcohol consumption in stands as outdated and discriminatory, arguing they should be scrapped. In response to the controversy, the police unit stated that they had not intended to make a link between the disaster and the ongoing discussion about alcohol regulations.

A fan group emphasized that the Hillsborough disaster was not caused by alcohol, distinguishing the historical tragedy from the current legislative debate. The UK Football Policing Unit maintained that no such connection was intended in their communications regarding the potential changes to drinking laws in English football.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Russell aims to keep fighting in F1 title race after fastest practice in Baku
content:
George Russell has vowed to continue his pursuit of the Formula One world championship despite trailing his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli by 81 points. The British driver stated his goal is to win every remaining race, a stance he began to support by recording the fastest time in practice for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The race in Baku is scheduled for Saturday to avoid a clash with Azerbaijan’s national remembrance day.

Antonelli currently holds an advantage in the standings, having secured eight victories this season, including the two most recent races. The Italian driver won from 19th on the grid in Monza and subsequently took the flag in Madrid. Russell remains in the title race, insisting he will keep fighting until the championship is mathematically out of reach.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Andy Carroll reveals 2021 sexual assault in autobiography
content:
Former England forward Andy Carroll has disclosed in his autobiography, *Owning It*, that he was sexually assaulted by a man at his home in 2021. The 37-year-old stated that the incident occurred during a second spell at Newcastle, when a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time, attacked him while he slept. Although Carroll was automatically granted anonymity as a victim of sexual assault, he chose to share the details in his book.

The attacker was found guilty of sexual offences after Carroll testified in court. Following the conviction, the man was jailed for three years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Germany Midfield Analysis and Lennart Karl's Return in UEFA Nations League
content:
Thursday night’s UEFA Nations League fixtures feature matches between the Netherlands and Germany, as well as Portugal and Wales. The German squad’s midfield composition includes Felix Nmecha, Jamal Musiala, and Joshua Kimmich, with the latter providing experience and intelligence. Analysts have questioned whether the team possesses sufficient goal-scoring capability and can execute manager Klopp’s high-energy style without extensive training time, particularly given the timing at the end of tiring seasons.

Attention is also directed toward 18-year-old Lennart Karl, who is anticipated to return to the team soon. Karl was originally selected for the World Cup squad but missed the tournament due to injury and was swapped with Karim Adeyemi for workload management reasons. The upcoming Nations League games offer an opportunity to observe the tactical developments and player performances across these international competitions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Premier League seeks agreement with EFL on funding model
content:
The Premier League has signalled a strong desire to settle the ongoing funding dispute with the English Football League.  

League officials say they are working toward an agreement on the EFL’s funding model and aim to achieve a resolution as quickly as possible.  

The Premier League hopes to reach an agreement with the EFL over its funding model “as soon as possible.”
author: BBC Sport

title: FAA Head Denies Political Interference in Trump Arch Safety Review
content:
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) head Bryan Bedford stated that there was no political interference in the air safety review for President Trump’s proposed triumphal arch. The review concluded that a visible eternal flame should be installed at the top of the structure.

Bedford explained that the process underwent the same obstruction evaluation that career employees conduct for such projects. The FAA’s assessment focused on ensuring the safety of the proposed design.
author: The Hill

title: FAA Blames Error Messages for Northeast Airport Flight Outage
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) attributed the recent flight halts at multiple northeast airports to error messages that prompted a switch to a backup fiber line. The agency stated that it was advised on Sunday by technology contractor L3Harris to make the switch in order to begin troubleshooting at a Philadelphia location.

This action resulted in the suspension of flights at several airports in the region, with the FAA citing the initial error messages as the root cause for the operational disruption.
author: The Hill

title: Mexico’s USMCA violations threaten American energy
content:
U.S. and Mexican trade officials are scheduled to meet in Washington this month to discuss Mexico’s alleged violation of USMCA commitments. The primary focus of these negotiations will be addressing discriminatory energy policies that are currently in place in Mexico.

These upcoming discussions aim to resolve the specific trade concerns related to the North American Free Trade Agreement’s energy provisions. The meeting serves as a direct response to the identified violations of the agreement’s terms.
author: The Hill

title: State Department Orders Diplomats to Use 'Super Intelligence' Over 'Artificial Intelligence'
content: The State Department has instructed its diplomats to adopt the term “super intelligence” (SI) in place of “artificial intelligence” across all official communications, a directive issued following President Trump’s push for the terminology change, according to a report by The Associated Press on Wednesday. The news outlet disclosed an email with the subject line “Change in Nomenclature AI to SI” that was sent to the department’s Bureau of.
author: The Hill

title: Reasons Phone Weather Forecasts Can Be Inaccurate
content:
Weather forecasts displayed on mobile phone applications frequently fail to match actual weekend conditions, resulting in significant discrepancies between predicted and observed weather patterns. Users often encounter situations where the highs, lows, and probability of precipitation shown in their apps are entirely different from the reality experienced during the weekend.

These inaccuracies can manifest in various ways, such as rain occurring despite forecasts indicating dry weather or temperatures being substantially hotter than anticipated. The mismatch between the digital predictions and the physical weather events highlights the potential unreliability of the numerical data provided by these mobile services.
author: The Hill

title: CNN Poll: 75% of Americans Fear AI Development
content:
A majority of Americans are worried about the progress of artificial intelligence, with tech industry leaders and lawmakers simultaneously calling for a slowdown in its development, according to a poll released Thursday. The CNN survey found that three-quarters of respondents reported some level of “fear and concern” regarding the “growth and development of AI technology.”

The remaining 25 percent of respondents did not report such fear or concern in the new survey.
author: The Hill

title: Harmeet Dhillon Accuses UC School of Racial Discrimination
content: Harmeet Dhillon has accused a University of California school of discriminating against white and Asian students. The content asserts that higher education admissions officers seek to select students based on skin color, although such practices are no longer permitted.
author: The Hill

title: NY congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier arrested at UN protest
content: New York congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier (D) was arrested on Thursday during a protest against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speech at the United Nations. Avila Chevalier is all but assured to win Rep. Adiriano Espaillat’s (D-N. Y.) blue House seat after besting him in this year’s primary. She was among roughly a group of individuals involved in the demonstration.
author: The Hill

title: Glasgow City Council to fire and rehire over 23,000 employees
content: Glasgow City Council has announced plans to fire and rehire more than 23,000 of its employees. The council stated that redundancy notices would be withdrawn if the three involved unions agree to ballot their members regarding the pay offer.
author: BBC Politics

title: Ministers reject dog ownership licence scheme
content:
Ministers have turned down a proposal to introduce a licence scheme for dog owners, rejecting the plan that had been put forward as a new legal requirement. The decision was announced after a taskforce had suggested that such measures could help promote dog control and reduce attacks.

The taskforce’s recommendation centered on the idea that additional legal requirements would improve public safety by encouraging responsible ownership and lowering the incidence of dog‑related incidents. Despite the taskforce’s arguments, the ministers chose not to adopt the licence scheme.

Ministers rejected the dog ownership licence scheme, and the taskforce had suggested new legal requirements could help promote dog control and reduce attacks.
author: BBC Politics

title: Kenya President and British envoy push for clean cooking in COP31 electrification agenda
content:
The President of Kenya and the British climate envoy have stated that Africa should leverage the global electrification push to implement clean cooking solutions. This advocacy aims to integrate cooking into the broader electrification agenda at COP31.

The two officials emphasized the importance of including this specific energy sector in international climate discussions. Their comments highlight a strategic approach to addressing energy access in Africa through electrification. This joint position underscores the role of high-level diplomatic engagement in shaping the COP31 agenda.
author: Climate Home News

title: Rick Wakeman Plays Piano for 150 Rescued Moon Bears in Vietnam
content:
Former Yes musician Rick Wakeman performed a piano concert for an audience of 150 rescued moon bears at a sanctuary in Vietnam. The event was organized to raise awareness for animals that remain trapped in cages at “bile farms.” This performance marked a unique experience for Wakeman, who has previously played for various audiences around the globe but had never encountered a bear enclosure before.

Wakeman, known for his prolific solo career following his time with Yes, played the piano specifically for the bears at the Vietnamese facility. The concert served as a highlight for the sanctuary, drawing attention to the plight of the animals still held in captivity.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Gavin Newsom condemns Democrats’ ‘climate hushing’, predicts Trump’s downfall and expects AOC to run in 2028
content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom criticized Democratic politicians for avoiding discussions on climate change, a practice he termed “climate hushing,” arguing that the issue is often ignored because candidates lack the skills to connect environmental shocks to everyday “kitchen table” concerns. Speaking during an interview with the Guardian and Covering Climate Now on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and New York Climate Week, Newsom emphasized the necessity for the party to articulate the direct impact of climate change on voters.

The governor also forecast that the upcoming November midterm elections would mark “the end of Donald Trump’s presidency as we know it,” urging voters to turn out in such overwhelming numbers that any attempt by Trump to contest the results would be impossible. Newsom stated that if the US president declares a national emergency or attempts to invalidate the outcome, the courts must intervene and Congress must stand up for the rule of law to ensure the democratic process is upheld.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Healthcare's high-stakes game of brinkmanship threatens patient care
content: For most Americans with private health insurance, hospital prices are not set by the government. Instead, these costs are determined through negotiations between hospitals and insurers, who agree on the payment amounts when an insurer’s members receive care.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cedars-Sinai researchers identify enzyme to prevent liver disease progression
content:
A preclinical study co-led by investigators from Cedars-Sinai Health Sciences University has identified an enzyme that helps prevent the most common form of liver disease from progressing toward liver failure. The findings, published in Nature Metabolism, suggest that restoring the enzyme involved in cellular cleanup could reduce inflammation and scarring associated with metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

The research indicates that this specific enzyme plays a critical role in halting the advancement of liver disease. By targeting this mechanism, the study results could point the way to new approaches for preventing serious organ damage.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Immunosuppressed cancer patients on checkpoint inhibitors face higher risk of severe infections
content:
A recent retrospective study from the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute indicates that patients who are heavily immunosuppressed while receiving anticancer immunotherapy face a heightened risk of serious infections. The research focuses on the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), which are known to stimulate antitumor activity but can also trigger adverse effects that necessitate treatment with immunosuppressive drugs.

The investigators found that patients who received ICIs in combination with multiple immunosuppressive therapies were more likely to develop serious infections. Nearly half of these infections were severe, life‑threatening, or fatal. The findings are reported in the Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network.

The study demonstrates that patients treated with ICIs and multiple immunosuppressive therapies face a higher risk of serious infections, with almost half of those infections being severe, life‑threatening, or fatal, as published in the Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experimental chemotherapy uses stealth tactic to activate inside cancer cells
content:
UC Irvine researchers are developing an experimental chemotherapy approach designed to mitigate the damage healthy tissue typically suffers from potent cancer drugs. The team is implementing a safety lock on a highly effective medication, ensuring it remains inactive until it reaches its intended target. This mechanism is specifically engineered to respond to the internal environment of cancer cells that exhibit high levels of protein-destroying activity.

The proposed solution addresses the fundamental challenge of chemotherapy by allowing the drug to activate only after entering these specific cancer cells. By restricting the drug's potency to the tumor site, the method aims to preserve the integrity of surrounding healthy tissue. This stealth tactic represents a targeted strategy to enhance the safety profile of existing powerful cancer treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: White House allows CNN, MS Now, and Politico journalists back after judge's ruling
content:
Journalists from CNN, MS Now, and Politico were granted access to the White House on Thursday afternoon, following a federal judge’s ruling that the Trump administration must allow them back after a ban was imposed. This development occurred many hours after the initial ruling, as earlier attempts by the journalists to enter the building had been unsuccessful.

The situation had escalated after the outlets requested an emergency hearing, with lawyers for the three organizations informing the judge that the White House had repeatedly violated his overnight order. That order required the Trump administration to return the press badges of the journalists from the three news organizations.
author: Guardian Business

title: US Mortgage Rates Exceed 7% for First Time in 20 Months
content:
US mortgage rates exceeded 7% for the first time since January 2025, according to federal lender Freddie Mac. This rise exacerbates a housing market that has faced years of high interest rates and low supply, occurring as Americans contend with elevated prices and stagnant wages.

The rate increase follows a decision by the US Federal Reserve to hike interest rates, a move that directly influences mortgage costs. The Federal Reserve cited high inflation as the reason for this adjustment, which marks the first rate hike since 2023.
author: Guardian Business

title: EU warns Trump diesel export ban would hurt Europe and US
content: The European Commission has expressed concern over reports that US President Donald Trump may implement a 90-day ban on US diesel exports ahead of the midterm elections. The EU warned that such a move would negatively impact both Europe and the US, noting that restricting diesel from reaching the global market could lead to even higher fuel prices across Europe.
author: Guardian Business

title: Learning Styles Predict Survival Skills in Young Orangutans
content:
Orangutan infants remain with their mothers for the first eight years of their lives, a period during which they can draw on their mothers' knowledge. Following this extended dependency phase, orangutans become entirely independent and must rely on their own abilities to survive.

To fare well as independent individuals, young orangutans are required to acquire numerous survival skills, with feeding skills identified as arguably the most important. This transition from maternal reliance to self-sufficiency necessitates the development of these critical competencies for long-term survival.
author: Phys.org

title: Study Finds Lactose-Intolerant Consumers Pay Premium for Lactose-Free Ice Cream
content:
A study led by researchers at Penn State and the University of Wisconsin indicates that lactose-intolerant consumers are willing to pay a premium for lactose-free ice cream. The research highlights a potential expanded market for lactose-free or reduced-lactose products, given that an estimated 36% of people in the United States have some degree of lactose intolerance.

This market opportunity is particularly relevant if individuals with lactose intolerance continue to accept higher prices for such specialized items. The findings from the Penn State and University of Wisconsin researchers suggest that consumer willingness to pay more supports the viability of these products in the broader ice cream market.
author: Phys.org

title: Dog brains track consonant patterns in speech, a first outside humans
content:
A new study from Hungary reveals that dog brains segment speech into words in a manner previously observed only in humans. This finding indicates that efficient speech processing is not exclusively a result of unique human language abilities, suggesting instead that regular exposure to speech can reshape brain function in mammalian species evolutionarily distant from humans.

The research, conducted by the Neuroethology of Communication Lab at the ELTE Department of Ethology in Budapest, demonstrates that dog brains track consonant patterns in speech. This discovery, which marks the first instance of such processing identified outside of humans, has been published in the journal Science.
author: Phys.org

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Method Improves Investment Selection
content:
Researchers have proposed a hybrid quantum-classical method to improve the selection of profitable investments from large and constrained asset pools, as reported in the International Journal of Information and Communication Technology. This approach aims to address a significant computational challenge within modern portfolio management.

The study suggests that combining quantum and classical computing techniques could make investment selection more effective by handling the complexity of increasingly large asset options. This hybrid method is presented as a potential solution to the major computational problems inherent in managing modern portfolios.
author: Phys.org

title: Ritual baths found at foot of Jerusalem's Temple Mount
content:
A monumental complex of ritual baths has been uncovered at the foot of the Temple Mount, likely serving as a place for Jewish pilgrims to purify themselves before entering the Temple in Jerusalem. The exceptionally well-preserved structure dates to the late Second Temple period, spanning from the first century BCE to 70 CE.

The complex features three large ritual baths, known as mikva'ot, along with a monumental plastered pool, a paved plaza, and an extensive water system. These findings provide physical evidence of the purification practices associated with visits to the Temple during that historical era.
author: Phys.org

title: Arctic Sea Ice Hits 2026 Annual Minimum Extent
content: Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on September 12, according to data from NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) at the University of Colorado Boulder. The ice covered an estimated 1.78 million square miles (4.6 million square kilometers), a figure that ties 2008, 2010, and 2025 for the 10th-lowest minimum in the satellite record.
author: Phys.org

title: Short peptides self-assemble into honeycomb fibers holding water
content:
Researchers have developed short peptides that self-assemble into honeycomb-shaped structures on a microscopic scale. These molecules, composed of only nine amino acids, form tiny fibers with a honeycomb-like interior that holds water within parallel channels.

This design mimics the familiar geometry of beehives but operates at a scale invisible to the naked eye. The resulting structures consist of many identical peptide copies organized into fibers filled with water.
author: Phys.org

title: Backpack Uses Electrodes to Massage Fatigued Back Muscles
content:
A new backpack equipped with electrodes, cables, and a soft massage head is designed to automatically knead back muscles upon detecting signs of fatigue. The device integrates these components to provide targeted relief directly to the user’s back.

This innovative accessory serves as an active tool for managing muscle tiredness by responding to specific physiological signals.
author: New Scientist

title: Dogs Focus on Consonants in Human Speech
content: Connecting dogs to non-invasive EEG monitors has allowed researchers to identify the specific components of human speech to which the animals are most attuned. This method facilitated the observation of canine attention patterns during exposure to spoken language. The findings indicate that dogs pay more attention to consonants than vowels when humans speak.
author: New Scientist

title: Young Orangutans Learn Diet by Copying Others
content:
Young orangutans rely on imitation to expand their dietary repertoire, a strategy that helps them learn which foods are suitable for consumption. Recent research indicates that copying the foraging choices of older individuals can guide juveniles toward a more varied diet. This behavior appears to be a key component of the species’ learning process.

The study notes that orangutans require more than eight years to acquire the skills needed to survive independently. During this extended period, they observe and replicate the feeding habits of their peers and caregivers. Scientists now have a clearer understanding of the mechanisms by which these primates determine which foods to add to their diet.

Orangutans spend more than eight years learning how to cope on their own, and now we have a clearer idea of how they work out which foods to incorporate into their diet.
author: New Scientist

title: MIT handheld device collects living cells to aid early cancer detection
content:
A new cell‑collection device could improve early cancer detection, according to a recent development announced by researchers at MIT. The handheld system is designed to gently collect living cells from patient samples, offering a novel tool for cancer testing.

The MIT team created the portable device to aid in the testing of cancer and the development of personalized medicines. By extracting viable cells without causing damage, the system aims to support more accurate diagnostic procedures and tailored therapeutic approaches.

The handheld system gently collects living cells from patient samples to aid cancer testing and development of personalized medicines.
author: MIT News

title: Google’s Project Suncatcher to put ML infrastructure in space
content:
Google’s Project Suncatcher aims to place machine learning infrastructure in space, according to a report by The New York Times. The initiative is designed to leverage orbital positioning for computational tasks, marking a distinct approach to deploying artificial intelligence resources beyond Earth’s surface.

The project has generated discussion within the technology community, as evidenced by its presence on Hacker News where it accumulated 27 points and 36 comments. This reaction highlights the significant interest and debate surrounding the feasibility and implications of moving data center operations into orbit.
author: Hacker News

title: Whiteboard Launches as Open-Source IDE for Collaborative Software Design
content:
Sid, Alex, Ketan, and Milan have released Whiteboard, an open-source desktop application designed to allow humans and AI agents to architect software together in a shared workspace. The team, who previously worked as tech leads, developed the tool to address the "cognitive debt" they experienced when maintaining codebases created by agentic coding tools. Whiteboard integrates with existing tools such as Claude Code and Codex, providing an SDK that enables agents to draw on an in-app canvas to describe their work. The application is built on CodeOSS, allowing users to click on visualizations like sequence diagrams or entity relationship diagrams to jump directly to the underlying code with VSCode keybindings and LSP support.

The platform includes a semantic, AST-aware diff viewer written in Rust that filters code changes to show only relevant updates, such as summarizing large added functions as pseudocode. It also features a Decision Log that allows agents to link their autonomous traces to the Whiteboard, helping users understand how specific requirements were implemented. Companies including Salesforce and Modal are currently using Whiteboard as a review tool for architecture or spec-level changes, often combining it with automated code reviewers like Greptile to escalate complex changes for human judgment.

The developers, who are college buddies that quit their jobs before agentic coding became standard, are releasing the desktop app under an MIT license for MacOS and Linux. They plan to eventually charge companies for a hosted web version that includes trajectory storage and multiplayer reviews, while keeping the software self-hostable. The project is available for contribution on GitHub, and the team welcomes feedback from the community.
